steps: Decide which calculation it is: gas volume, atom economy, or percentage yield
Gas volume at RTP: volume = moles × 24 (and moles = volume ÷ 24)
Atom economy: (Mr of desired product ÷ total Mr of reactants) × 100
method_card.title: Gas Volumes, Atom Economy and Percentage Yield
method_card.content: Three separate calculations. Gas volume at RTP: one mole of any gas fills 24 dm³, so \(V = \text{moles} \times 24\) (and \(\text{moles} = V \div 24\)). Atom economy is about the balanced equation: \((M_r\text{ desired} \div \text{total } M_r\text{ reactants}) \times 100\). Percentage yield is about the experiment: \((\text{actual} \div \text{theoretical}) \times 100\), and can never exceed 100%. Remember 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³.

steps: Multi-step problems link mass, moles, ratio and volume. Do one step at a time and keep a unit beside every number.
For a yield from a gas, find the theoretical volume, then convert: 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³ before comparing.
For competing routes, only use the reactants of the route named in the question.
